long_description:
D7571 - Battery Voltage Out Of Range Low

Detailed Description

A Code D7571 occurs when the Drive Controller detects a voltage less than 9.1 volts on the un-switched power supply from the battery. If Code D7571 occurs, the drive functions will be disabled.

Possible Causes

  • FC1 Fuse 4.
  • Supply wire 1250 or 1260 shorted to ground or open.
  • Ground wire 2040 or 2490 open.
  • Battery.
  • Alternator.
  • Drive Controller.
  • Moisture, corrosion, or pushed back pins in the Drive Controller connectors, Alternator connector, Main Frame harness, SJC harness connectors. See Electrical Systems Connector Maintenance in Technical Information.
  • If the code is intermittent and not on at the time of testing, the cause of the code may not be found at this time. Probable causes may include: loose connections, corrosion, pushed back pins, the controller, the wire harness or a combination of these problems. Refer to Troubleshooting Intermittent Electrical Faults Procedures in Technical Information.

Conditions for Alarm

  • Key switch / (run/enter) On.

Conditions for Clearing Alarm

  • Self Resetting.

Detailed Description

A Code D7588 occurs when the Drive / Drive Plus Controller detects that the switched power to the Drive / Drive Plus Controller has remained on for 2 minutes or more after the machine has been shutdown. Additional codes D7540 or D7542 may also occur.

  • Drive Controller.

Refer to Troubleshooting Intermittent Electrical Faults Procedures in Technical Information.

D7578 - Right Speed Sensor Out Of Range High

Detailed Description

A Code D7578 occurs when the Drive Controller detects that the pulses from the Right Speed sensor are greater than 4.85 volts. This information is used by the Drive Controller to detect machine movement and speed. If a Code D7578 occurs, the machine will operate in Speed Management Mode. A wheel machine has sensors in the motor carriers that detect magnets on a rotating disk. A track machine has the sensors in the drive motors that detect the teeth on a metal sprocket.

Possible Causes

  • Signal wire (3000 or 3870) or signal wire (3070 or 3875) shorted to supply voltage.
  • 5 volt supply wire 5870 shorted to supply voltage.
  • Ground wire 2870 open.
  • Right Speed sensor.
  • Drive Controller.
  • Moisture, corrosion, or pushed back pins in the Drive Controller connectors or SJC harness connectors. See Electrical Systems Connector Maintenance in Technical Information.
  • If the code is intermittent and not on at the time of testing, the cause of the code may not be found at this time. Probable causes may include: loose connections, corrosion, pushed back pins, the controller, the wire harness or a combination of these problems. Refer to Troubleshooting Intermittent Electrical Faults Procedures in Technical Information.

Conditions for Alarm

  • Key switch / (run/enter) On.

Conditions for Clearing Alarm

  • Self Resetting.

A Code D7554 occurs if the Drive / Drive Plus Controller does not detect voltage to the Left Reverse Drive solenoid when commanded. The Drive / Drive Plus Controller will vary the voltage on the drive solenoids with respect to the signal inputs from the joysticks. If a Code D7554 occurs, the Loader will operate in Speed Management Mode.

  • Left Reverse Drive solenoid.
  • Drive / Drive Plus Controller.
  • Moisture, corrosion, or pushed back pins in the Drive / Drive Plus Controller connectors, Left Reverse Drive solenoid connector, or AWS / SJC wire harness. See Electrical Systems Connector Maintenance in Technical Information.

Probable causes may include: loose connections, corrosion, pushed back pins, the controller, the wire harness or a combination of these problems. Refer to Troubleshooting Intermittent Electrical Faults Procedures in Technical Information.

long_description:
D7518 - Right Swash Plate Not In Neutral

Detailed Description

A Code D7518 occurs when the Drive Controller detects the Right Swash Plate sensor is not in the neutral range of 2.08 – 2.92 volts. When the PTOL is enabled, the Drive Controller will monitor the position of the Swash Plate sensors. The Swash Plate sensors are located at the bottom of the pump and are keyed to the swash plate inside the pump. Swash Plate sensors provide feedback to the Drive Controller on the position of the swash plate inside the pump. The Swash Plate sensor is supplied battery voltage from the Gateway Controller, but the Swash Plate output signal range is 1.0 to 4.0 volts. This code will only occur at the system start up, not during normal operation. If a Code D7518 occurs, the engine will shutdown.

Possible Causes

  • Contamination of the hydraulic system.
  • Hydraulic pump is not physically centered. Refer to the Service Manual.
  • Right Swash Plate sensor.
  • Drive Controller.
  • Moisture, corrosion, or pushed back pins in the Drive Controller connectors, Swash Plate sensor connector, or SJC wire harness. See Electrical Systems Connector Maintenance in Technical Information.
  • If the code is intermittent and not on at the time of testing, the cause of the code may not be found at this time. Probable causes may include: loose connections, corrosion, pushed back pins, the controller, the wire harness or a combination of these problems. Refer to Troubleshooting Intermittent Electrical Faults Procedures in Technical Information.

Conditions for Alarm

  • Key switch / (run/enter) On.

Conditions for Clearing Alarm

  • Cycle power.

long_description:
D7572 - Drive Pump – Not Calibrated

Detailed Description

A Code D7572 occurs when an uncalibrated Drive / Drive Plus Controller is installed in a machine, or when a calibration of the Drive / Drive Plus Controller fails. Other causes for the code are when the upgrade to the Drive / Drive Plus Controller is interrupted, causing the information to be corrupt, or if the wrong software is installed in the controller.

Possible Causes

  • Drive / Drive Plus Controller needs calibration.
  • Engine Speed sensor.
  • Wheel Speed sensors.
  • Swash Plate sensor.
  • Drive Pump solenoids.
  • Contamination in the hydraulic system.
  • Drive / Drive Plus Controller.
  • Power or communication loss during software update to the Drive / Drive Plus Controller.
  • Wrong software downloaded into Drive / Drive Plus Controller.
  • Moisture, corrosion, or pushed back pins in the Drive / Drive Plus Controller connectors or AWS / SJC harness connectors. See Electrical Systems Connector Maintenance in Technical Information.
  • If the code is intermittent and not on at the time of testing, the cause of the code may not be found at this time. Probable causes may include: loose connections, corrosion, pushed back pins, the controller, the wire harness or a combination of these problems. Refer to Troubleshooting Intermittent Electrical Faults Procedures in Technical Information.

Conditions for Alarm

  • Key switch / (run/enter) On.

Conditions for Clearing Alarm

  • N/A.
title: D7572
